source_text: ρὸν εἰς ἀγγεῖον ὀστράκινον ἐνίεσθαι δεῖν, καὶ μὴν καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς τῆς οὔσης ἐπὶ τῆς σκηνῆς. Εἶτα τῶν τῆς ἀρᾶς λόγων ἐναποπλυνθέντων ὕδατι, πίνειν ἐκέλευσε τὴν ἐν ὑποψίαις τοῦ πεπορνεῦσθαι γυναῖκα. Καὶ, «Εἰ μὲν ἔνοχος εἴη τῷ ἐγκλήματι, πρησθήσεται,» φησὶ, «κοιλίαν, καὶ πεσεῖται μηρός· εἰ δὲ τῆς αἰτίας ἀπήλλακται, καὶ οὐκ ἀληθὲς ἐπ' αὐτῇ τὸ ὑπειλημμένον, ἐκσπερματιεῖ σπέρμα.» {ΠΑΛΛ.} Τίς οὖν ὁ λόγος; ἢ πῶς ἂν ἡμῖν καὶ διὰ τῶν ἀρτίως ὠνομασμένων, ὁ Χριστὸς σημαίνοιτο; {ΚΥΡ.} Διὰ μὲν γὰρ τοῦ ὕδατος τοῦ ζῶντος καὶ καθαροῦ, τὸν ζωοποιὸν συνήσεις τὸν Θεοῦ Λόγον, τὸν ἀληθῶς καθαρὸν, καὶ ἁμαρτίας ἀμέτοχον παντελῶς, ὃς ἐν σαρκὶ γέγονε, καθάπερ ἐν ὀστρακίνῳ σκεύει. Χοῦς γὰρ ὅτι καὶ ἀπὸ γῆς ἡ σὰρξ, πῶς ἂν ἢ πόθεν ἀμφίβολον; Διὰ δέ γε τῆς ἀπὸ τῆς σκηνῆς γῆς, τὸν ἐν θανάτῳ νοήσεις δι' ἡμᾶς· εἴρηται γὰρ τῇ ἀνθρώπου φύσει· «Γῆ εἶ, καὶ εἰς γῆν ἀπελεύσῃ.» Διὰ δέ γε τῶν λόγων τῆς ἀρᾶς, τὸν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν γεγονότα κατάραν, διὰ τὸ ἐπὶ ξύλου κρεμασθῆναι, συνήσεις εὖ μάλα. Γέγραπται γὰρ, ὅτι καὶ «Ἐπικατάρατος πᾶς ὁ κρεμάμενος ἐπὶ ξύλου.» Ὅταν τοίνυν εἰς τὸ τῆς ἀνθρωπίνης διανοίας καθίκοιτο βάθος, Θεὸς κατὰ φύσιν ὑπάρχων ὁ Ἐμμανουὴλ, ἐνόχους μὲν ὄντας πταίσμασιν, ἐλέγξει κολάζων· κατειλημμένους δὲ οὐκ ἐν τούτοις, καρποφόρους ἀποφανεῖ. Τοῦτο γὰρ, οἶμαι, ἐστὶ τὸ, ἐκσπερματιεῖ σπέρμα, τῆς ψυχῆς τὸ καρπογόνον, τοῦ σωματικοῦ σημαίνοντος πάθους. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἄριστα ἔφης. {ΚΥΡ.} Πορνεία μὲν οὖν καὶ τὰ σαρκὸς πάθη κατακιβδηλεύει τὸν ἄνθρωπον, καὶ τῆς πρὸς Θεὸν ἐξίστησιν οἰκειότητος· οἱ γὰρ ἐν σαρκὶ ὄντες, Θεῷ ἀρέσαι οὐ δύνανται. Σάρκα δὲ, καθάπερ ἐγᾦμαι, τὸ σαρκικὸν ὀνομάζει φρόνημα. Νοοῖτο γὰρ ἂν ὡδὶ τὸ γεγραμμένον ὀρθῶς. Τρόπος δὲ αὖ πρὸς τόδε φαυλότητος, καὶ μὴν καὶ ἠθῶν ῥυθμὸς ἀγριότητος, καὶ εἰς πᾶν ὁτιοῦν τῶν ἐκτοπωτάτων ἐξιτηλία, βδελυροὺς ἡμᾶς καὶ ἀνιέρους ἀποτελεῖ. Οὐ γάρ τοι προσήκει σαρκικῶν ἡμᾶς μόνων κατανδρίζεσθαι παθῶν, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἠθῶν ἡμερότητι διαπρέπειν, καὶ ἀγάπης ὅτι μάλιστα τῆς εἰς ἀδελφοὺς ἐπιμελητὰς ἀναφαίνεσθαι, καὶ τοῖς τῆς δικαιοσύνης αὐχήμασιν ὁρᾶσθαι κατεστεμμένους, καὶ πρός γε δὴ τούτοις, λεπτὸν καὶ ἐξησκημένον ἔν γε δὴ σφίσιν αὐτοῖς ἔχειν τὸν νοῦν, ταῖς περὶ Θεοῦ δόξαις ἀδιαστρόφως προσβάλλοντα, καὶ ἐν δογμάτων ἐρεύναις πανταχῆ σώζοντα τὸ ἀμωμήτως ἔχον· τέλειοι γὰρ οἱ τοιοίδε, κατὰ τὸ ἀληθὲς οὐδενὸς ὄντες τῶν ἀρίστων ἐπιδεεῖς· ἄρτιον γὰρ εἶναι δεῖν τὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἄνθρωπον καὶ ὁ θεῖος ἡμῖν ἔφη Παῦλος· «Ἄρτιον» δέ φησι τὸν εἰς πᾶν ἔργον ἀγαθὸν ἐξηρτυμένον, καὶ ἐπιτηδείως ἔχοντα πρὸς τὸ κατορθοῦν εὖ μάλα δύνασθαι τὴν ἀρετήν. Ἢ οὐχ ὧδε ἔχει; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Πῶς γὰρ οὔ; {ΚΥΡ.} Θέα δὴ οὖν ὅπως αἰνιγματωδῶς ὁ νόμος εἰς
pass_a_gloss: [Cyril, continuing] …(living and) pure water must be put into an earthen vessel, and also from the earth that is upon/in the tent. Then, the words of the curse having been washed off into water, he ordered the woman in suspicions of having fornicated to drink. And: if she should be liable to the charge, she will be swollen as to the belly, and the thigh will fall; but if she has been freed of the accusation, and what was supposed of her is not true, she will conceive offspring. [Palladius] What then is the meaning? Or how would Christ be signified to us through the things just named? [Cyril] Through the living and pure water you will understand the life-making Word of God, the truly pure, wholly without share of sin, who came to be in flesh as in an earthen vessel. That the flesh is dust and from earth, how or whence doubtful? Through the earth from the tent you will think of the one in death for our sake; for it was said to the nature of man: Earth you are, and to earth you will go away. Through the words of the curse you will understand very well the one who became a curse for us through being hung on wood. For it is written: Cursed is everyone hanging on wood. Whenever, then, Emmanuel, being God by nature, should come down into the depth of the human mind, those liable to faults he will convict by punishing; those not caught in these he will show fruit-bearing. For this, I think, is the ‘she will conceive offspring’: the bodily experience signifying the fruit-producing of the soul. [Palladius] You spoke excellently. [Cyril] Fornication and the passions of the flesh debase/adulterate the human being and remove him from intimacy with God; for those in the flesh cannot please God. Flesh, as I suppose, he names the fleshly mind; for so the written text would be rightly understood. And again besides this, a manner of wickedness, a rhythm/cast of habits of savagery, and a lapsing into anything whatever of the most outlandish, render us loathsome and unholy. For it is not fitting for us to play the man against fleshly passions only, but also to excel in gentleness of habits, and to appear most of all as carers of love toward brothers, and to be seen crowned with the boasts/glories of righteousness, and besides, to have within themselves a mind fine and trained, applying to the opinions about God undistortedly, and in searches of doctrines everywhere preserving the blameless; for such are perfect, truly lacking none of the best things; for the divine Paul too said that the man of God must be complete; complete he calls the one equipped for every good work, and suited to be able to achieve virtue very well. Or is it not so? [Palladius] How not? [Cyril] Look, then, how in riddling fashion the law, for… [continues in §16]
pass_b_english: Cyril: …pure water must be poured into an earthen vessel, together with some of the earth that lies in the tent (Numbers 5:17). Then, when the words of the curse had been washed off into the water, he commanded the woman suspected of fornication to drink it (Numbers 5:23–24). And he says: ‘If she is guilty of the charge, her belly will swell and her thigh will fall away; but if she is clear of the accusation, and what was suspected of her is not true, she will conceive offspring.’ (Numbers 5:27–28)
Palladius: What, then, is the meaning? Or how would Christ be signified to us even through the things just named?

Cyril: By the living and pure water you will understand the life-giving Word of God, who is truly pure and has no share in sin at all, and who came to be in flesh as in an earthen vessel. For how, or on what ground, could anyone doubt that the flesh is dust and comes from the earth? By the earth from the tent you will understand him who was in death for our sake; for it was said to human nature: ‘You are earth, and to earth you shall return.’ (Genesis 3:19) And by the words of the curse you will understand very well him who became a curse for us by being hung on a tree (Galatians 3:13). For it is written: ‘Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree.’ (Galatians 3:13; Deuteronomy 21:23) So when Emmanuel, who is God by nature, reaches down into the depth of the human mind, he will convict and punish those who are guilty of sins; but those who are not caught in them he will show to be fruitful. For this, I think, is the meaning of ‘she will conceive offspring’: the bodily experience signifies the fruitfulness of the soul.

Cyril: Fornication, then, and the passions of the flesh debase a person and drive him out of his closeness to God; for ‘those who are in the flesh cannot please God.’ (Romans 8:8) By ‘flesh,’ as I take it, he means the mind set on the flesh (Romans 8:6–7); for that is how the text would rightly be understood. And besides this, a wicked disposition, a savage cast of character, and a drift into anything whatever of the most monstrous kind make us loathsome and unholy. For it befits us not only to master the passions of the flesh, but also to excel in gentleness of character, to show ourselves above all diligent in love toward the brothers, to be seen crowned with the glories of righteousness, and besides this to keep within ourselves a mind that is keen and well trained, that approaches the teachings about God without distortion, and that in searching into doctrines keeps what is blameless at every point. For such people are perfect, since in truth they lack none of the highest goods. The divine Paul also told us that the man of God must be complete (2 Timothy 3:17); and by ‘complete’ he means one who is equipped for every good work and well fitted to achieve virtue fully. Or is it not so?
Palladius: How could it not be?
Cyril: See, then, how the law, speaking in riddles,…

apparatus.note: Migne PG 68 print; the column break may cut a sentence or a word.

PG 68.913. Opens mid-word (καθα|ρόν) completing §14’s ‘For it said that living and…’. ἐπὶ τῆς σκηνῆς: Cyril’s short form of Numbers 5:17 ‘the earth on the floor of the tent’; rendered ‘the earth that lies in the tent’. The ‘quotation’ ‘If she is guilty… she will conceive offspring’ is Cyril’s paraphrase of Numbers 5:27–28, not the LXX wording; it is kept in quotation marks as the print has it. Genesis 3:19 LXX: γῆ εἶ καὶ εἰς γῆν ἀπελεύσῃ, quoted exactly. Galatians 3:13 quoted exactly (ἐπικατάρατος πᾶς ὁ κρεμάμενος ἐπὶ ξύλου); Paul there quotes Deuteronomy 21:23 (LXX κεκατηραμένος ὑπὸ θεοῦ), so both are cited. Romans 8:8 quoted exactly. ‘The fleshly mind’ (σαρκικὸν φρόνημα) echoes Romans 8:6–7 (τὸ φρόνημα τῆς σαρκός), cited as a clear allusion. 2 Timothy 3:17: Cyril’s ἐξηρτυμένον for NA ἐξηρτισμένος; sense the same. The earthen vessel for Christ’s flesh may echo 2 Corinthians 4:7 (ἐν ὀστρακίνοις σκεύεσιν) and ‘dust … from the earth’ Genesis 2:7; both doubtful, uncited. ‘Emmanuel’ is the title from Isaiah 7:14 and Matthew 1:23, used as a name, not quoted; uncited. καθίκοιτο εἰς … βάθος: ‘reaches down into the depth’, mirroring the water entering the woman’s belly. ἐλέγξει κολάζων rendered ‘convict and punish’. ἐξιτηλία is rare (from ἐξίτηλος, ‘fading, lapsing’); rendered ‘a drift into’; the sense (a sliding away into every vice) is clear from context, the exact nuance uncertain. ‘Brothers’ for ἀδελφούς (fellow believers). The section ends mid-sentence; the law is the subject of the participle and main verb that follow in §16 (παρενεγκὼν … ὀνίνησι).
